chunks: By this chain of narration. He said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) used to call out to the people three times in Kufa after leading the final Isha prayer, so that the people of the mosque could hear: "O people! Prepare yourselves, may Allah have mercy on you, for you have been called to departure. Why linger upon this world after you have been called to leave it! Prepare yourselves, may Allah have mercy on you, and move forth with the best provision at your disposal, and that is God-consciousness. Know that your path leads to the Return, your passage is over the Sirat, the greatest horror is before you, and upon your road is an arduous steep pass and terrifying, fearful stations that you must pass through and halt at. Either by the mercy of Allah you are delivered from their horror, the greatness of their danger, the severity of their appearance, and the intensity of their trial; or by destruction after which there is no recovery."

key_terms.التقوى: God-consciousness (taqwa) - the best provision for the afterlife
key_terms.الرحيل: Departure - metaphor for death and leaving this world
key_terms.الصراط: The Sirat - the bridge over Hell that all must cross on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.المعاد: The Return - the place of return to Allah in the afterlife

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about preparing for the afterlife in his sermon at Kufa?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (as) would deliver this powerful sermon nightly after Isha prayer in the mosque of Kufa during his caliphate, calling people to prepare for the afterlife. The sermon uses vivid metaphors of a perilous journey to warn against attachment to worldly life, emphasizing that God-consciousness (taqwa) is the best provision for the journey ahead.

en.bilal-muhammad: By this isnad. He said: Abu Ja`far (as) said:

When Amir al-Mu'minin (as) would lead the final `Isha’ prayer in Kufa, he would say this three times so that the people of the Mosque would hear it: "O people! Prepare yourselves, may Allah have mercy on you, for you have been called for departure. Do not confine yourself to this world after you have been called to leave it! Prepare yourselves, may Allah have mercy on you, with the best provision, and that is God-consciousness. Know that your road is toward the Resurrection, and you will pass over the Path (al-sirat). The great horror is before you, and upon your road is a severe obstacle and houses of horror and fear. You must pass through it and halt at it. If you receive a mercy from Allah, then you will be delivered from its horror, the greatness of its danger, and the severity of its trial. If there is destruction, then there is no solace after it."
